Daily Brief

The day's news is dominated by escalating tensions in the US-Iran conflict, with President Trump publicly rejecting Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz [BBC, Globe and Mail], while UK police declared a 'major incident' near RAF Fairford, arresting several men on explosives offenses near the base used for US strikes on Iran [France 24, The Hindu]. The Trump-Xi summit in Washington concluded with modest agreements on AI safety channels and military communications, though no major breakthroughs emerged [Globe and Mail, The Economist]. Pope Leo XIV drew an estimated 800,000 people to an open-air Mass on the Champs-Élysées, using the occasion to warn against the dangers of AI and address the Church's abuse crisis [BBC, Globe and Mail, RFI]. Violence continued to grip South Africa, where two mass shootings within hours left at least 27 dead near Johannesburg and Cape Town, prompting a police manhunt [BBC, Guardian, ABC Australia]. In Europe, Germany saw student strikes against potential military conscription [BBC], while Poland blamed Russia for sabotage at a Starlink station [BBC]. The EU announced €710 million in humanitarian aid, primarily for Africa [RFI].

Trump Rejects Iranian Proposal to Reopen Strait of Hormuz, Dismisses Tehran's Peace Offer

  • President Trump publicly rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and end hostilities, calling it 'not acceptable'
  • Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said Tehran would await an official US response, noting Trump's contradictory past statements, and maintained that only a 'negotiated solution' can end the conflict
  • The strait, through which roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas flows, has been effectively closed since war began in February 2026
  • Trump claimed the US has 'total control' of the strait despite ongoing disruptions to global oil prices

UK Police Declare Major Incident Near US Air Base Used for Iran Strikes, Multiple Arrests Made

  • British police arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offenses near RAF Fairford in southwest England, which the US has used to conduct strikes on Iranian missile sites
  • Army bomb disposal experts examined multiple vehicles while residents of nearby villages were evacuated
  • Around 30 emergency vehicles deployed to the scene; police said they believed the incident was 'contained'
